paper_title: Frog in the Pan: Continuous Information and
summary: Deprioritize. The paper (Frog in the Pan, Da, Gurun and Warachka, 2014) argues that momentum is stronger when a stock's past return built up through many small daily moves than through a few large jumps, and we tested a long-only version on a 415-name S&P 500 survivor universe over 2015-2025. The strategy earned a net CAGR of 11.87% against 12.71% for the equal-weight universe, with a Sharpe ratio of 0.58 against 0.65, and the edge over the equal-weight universe fails at 10 bps and holds in 0 of 2 sub-periods. The simulated fund economics are uncertain: P(NPV > 0) is 43% and the median incremental fee PV is -$496k versus the equal-weight universe fund. The recommendation rests mainly on negative historical performance and weak robustness, with an amber implementation reliability because 4 fields were assumed and 6 adapted.
